supporting_capabilities: CAP-004 (Risk Management — credit risk assessment, SVC-012)
CAP-005 (Compliance & Regulatory — KYC if new customer, AML property checks, SVC-014)
description: A personal customer applies for a residential mortgage to purchase or remortgage a UK residential property. The journey spans enquiry through to completion, crossing multiple capability boundaries. SVC-002 (Mortgage Service) owns the application lifecycle; SVC-012 (Risk Engine) provides credit scoring via async events; SVC-014 (KYC/AML) provides identity verification for new customers and AML property checks via async events.
regulatory_framework: FCA MCOB (Mortgages and Home Finance: Conduct of Business sourcebook)
EU Mortgage Credit Directive (MCD) as retained UK law
Money Laundering Regulations 2017 (MLR 2017) — AML property check

phases.name: Mortgage Enquiry
phases.description: Customer provides property details (address, purchase price, type), deposit amount, and income information. An automated affordability pre-check runs to indicate borrowing capacity. The customer selects a product (fixed, variable, or tracker rate). No credit check is performed at this stage.
key_activities: Customer submits property details: address, purchase price, property type (residential owner-occupier, remortgage)
Customer submits deposit amount and loan requirement
Customer provides basic income details (gross annual income, employment type)
Automated affordability pre-check: indicative LTV, stress-test at SVR+3%, indicative monthly payment
Product selection from available mortgage product range
Mortgage Enquiry started event published (EVT-020)
phases.entry_criteria: Customer is authenticated (existing customer) or completes basic registration. Property address is in England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland.
phases.exit_criteria: Affordability pre-check completed; indicative borrowing amount calculated; customer selects a product and proceeds to DIP.
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 4.7 (Initial Disclosure Document)
MCOB 11 (Responsible lending — pre-check indicator only)

phases.name: Decision in Principle (DIP)
phases.description: A formal but non-binding Decision in Principle is issued following a soft credit check (no footprint on customer's credit file), income verification, and preliminary affordability assessment. The DIP is valid for 90 days and is used by the customer to demonstrate borrowing capacity to estate agents and vendors. No commitment from either party.
key_activities: Customer confirms income details and employment status in full
Soft credit check requested from credit bureau (EVT-022 CreditCheckRequested, cross-capability to SVC-012)
SVC-012 returns credit score and preliminary credit decision (EVT-023 CreditCheckCompleted)
Affordability assessment created (ENT-013): stress test at MCOB 11 prescribed rate
LTV calculation validated against product criteria
DIP issued if credit score and affordability pass thresholds
DIP document generated and issued to customer (EVT-021 DIPIssued)
phases.entry_criteria: PH-009 completed. Customer proceeds from enquiry.
phases.exit_criteria: DIP issued (approved) or DIP declined. If approved: DIP valid for 90 days. Customer may proceed to full application within validity window.
phases.automation_level: full (automated credit check and affordability; human review only for edge cases)
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 5 (Pre-application illustration — European Standardised Information Sheet, ESIS)
MCOB 11.6 (Affordability assessment — soft check only at DIP stage)
ICO guidance: soft credit search does not leave a visible footprint

phases.name: Full Application
phases.description: The customer submits a full formal mortgage application. A hard credit check is performed (visible footprint on credit file). Employment and income are formally verified. Bank statements are submitted. The application enters the lender's processing queue.
key_activities: Customer submits full application form: personal details, property details, financial position
Hard credit check requested (EVT-022 CreditCheckRequested — hard check flag)
Credit check result returned (EVT-023 CreditCheckCompleted — full credit report)
Income verification: payslips, P60, or self-assessment returns collected
Bank statements (3 months minimum) submitted and reviewed for expenditure patterns
AML property checks initiated via SVC-014 (EVT-022 variant for AML)
Application status updated to 'full_application_submitted'
Full application date recorded
phases.entry_criteria: Valid DIP within 90-day window. Customer confirms they wish to proceed with full application.
phases.exit_criteria: Full application received, all required documents uploaded, hard credit check completed. Application moves to valuation queue.
phases.automation_level: semi-automated (automated credit check; manual document review)
phases.sla: Application accepted into queue within 1 business day of document submission
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 11.6 (Full affordability assessment with hard credit check)
MLR 2017 Regulation 27 — CDD for new customers (if not existing bank customer)
MCOB 5.7 (ESIS — binding illustration at full application stage)

phases.name: Valuation
phases.description: A property valuation is instructed by the bank. The type of valuation (desktop, drive-by, or full structural survey) is determined by the LTV ratio, property type, and risk policy. An external surveyor or automated valuation model (AVM) produces a valuation report. The valuation result gates progression to underwriting.
key_activities: Bank instructs valuation: desktop AVM for low LTV clean properties; drive-by or full for higher LTV or non-standard construction
Valuation instructed event published (EVT-024 ValuationInstructed)
External surveyor instructed (for physical valuations)
Valuation report received by SVC-002
Valuation report reviewed: valuation_amount vs. purchase_price
If valuation_amount < purchase_price: down-valuation exception path triggered
Valuation completed event published (EVT-025 ValuationCompleted)
phases.entry_criteria: Full application received and initial checks passed. Valuation fee paid by customer.
phases.exit_criteria: Valuation report received. Valuation_amount >= required loan amount (or exception path invoked for down-valuation).
phases.automation_level: automated for AVM desktop valuations; manual for physical surveys
phases.sla: Desktop AVM: same day. Drive-by: 2–3 business days. Full structural: 5–7 business days.
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 11.3.4 (Property valuation — lender must carry out valuation before lending)
RICS Valuation — Global Standards (Red Book) for physical valuations
Consumer Duty: customer notified of valuation outcome

phases.name: Underwriting
phases.description: A mortgage underwriter reviews the complete application pack: full application, credit report, affordability assessment, valuation report, income verification, and AML checks. The underwriter makes a final credit decision: approve, refer (additional information required), or decline.
key_activities: Underwriter assigned to application (PER-055 Mortgage Underwriter)
Underwriter reviews full application pack: income, credit, valuation, expenditure
Complex cases escalated to PER-051 (Credit Analyst) for structural review
Underwriter checks compliance: MCOB affordability rules, LTV within product limits, LTI within regulatory caps
Underwriter decision: approve / refer / decline
For 'refer': conditions documented and additional information requested from customer
Underwriting decision event published (EVT-026 MortgageUnderwritingCompleted)
phases.entry_criteria: Valuation completed. All documents received. Credit check completed. AML checks cleared.
phases.exit_criteria: Underwriting decision made: approve (proceed to PH-014), refer (pending additional information), or decline (journey ends; FOS signpost provided).
phases.automation_level: manual (underwriter-led with automated pre-checks and decisioning assist)
phases.sla: < 5 business days from receipt of complete application pack (MCOB SLA commitment)
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 11 (Responsible lending — full underwriting obligations)
FCA LTI cap: residential mortgages — no more than 15% of new lending above 4.5x LTI (PRA Policy Statement PS11/13)
MCOB 2.5A (Consumer Duty — fair value, products and services outcome)
Consumer Duty: decline notification must include signpost to FOS

phases.name: Mortgage Offer
phases.description: Following underwriting approval, a formal Mortgage Offer is issued to the customer and their solicitor/conveyancer. The offer sets out the loan amount, interest rate, term, and any conditions. The customer has a 7-day reflection period before accepting. The offer is valid for 6 months.
key_activities: Mortgage Offer document generated (ENT-015 MortgageOffer created)
Offer issued to customer and solicitor/conveyancer (EVT-027 MortgageOfferIssued)
Customer receives 7-day reflection period (MCOB 6.7 — binding offer with mandatory reflection period)
Customer reviews offer with solicitor/conveyancer
Customer formally accepts the offer (EVT-028 MortgageOfferAccepted)
Solicitor/conveyancer begins conveyancing process
phases.entry_criteria: Underwriting decision = approve. All conditions satisfied.
phases.exit_criteria: Customer has accepted the mortgage offer within the 6-month validity window.
channels: post (regulatory requirement for binding offer document)
phases.automation_level: automated offer generation; customer acceptance manual
phases.sla: Offer issued within 2 business days of underwriting approval
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 6.7 (Binding offer — 7-day reflection period mandatory)
MCOB 6.4 (Mortgage offer document — prescribed content)
Consumer Duty: offer document must be clear, fair, and not misleading

phases.name: Completion
phases.description: The solicitor/conveyancer completes the legal conveyancing process. On completion day, the bank releases mortgage funds via CHAPS to the solicitor. Legal title transfers. The mortgage account is opened on the core banking system. The customer becomes a mortgage borrower.
key_activities: Solicitor completes legal property transfer and Land Registry registration
Solicitor requests funds on completion day
Bank releases mortgage funds via CHAPS (same-day irrevocable payment)
MortgageCompleted event published (EVT-029)
Mortgage account opened in SVC-002 (ENT-016 MortgageAccount created)
MortgageAccountOpened event published (EVT-030)
Direct debit mandate established for monthly mortgage payments
Welcome pack issued to customer with account details, first payment date, FSCS information
phases.entry_criteria: Mortgage offer accepted. Solicitor confirms exchange of contracts. Completion date agreed.
phases.exit_criteria: CHAPS funds released. MortgageAccount created and active. First direct debit payment scheduled.
phases.automation_level: semi-automated (CHAPS release automated on solicitor request; account opening automated)
phases.sla: CHAPS funds released by 3pm on completion day (Bank of England CHAPS operating window)
regulatory_touchpoints: MCOB 13 (Arrears and repossessions — account must be set up correctly to avoid arrears triggers)
FSCS: mortgage account not covered by FSCS deposit protection (mortgage is a liability, not a deposit)
Land Registry: legal charge registered within 30 days of completion
CHAPS: irrevocable same-day settlement (Bank of England scheme rules)

alternative_paths.name: Remortgage (no purchase)
alternative_paths.description: Customer is remortgaging an existing property (not purchasing). No chain dependency, no purchase solicitor required. PH-012 valuation may be AVM-only. Completion involves redemption of existing mortgage and drawdown of new mortgage simultaneously.
key_differences: No purchase price — based on current property value
Existing mortgage balance used to calculate net equity
Completion: redemption statement from existing lender required

alternative_paths.name: Buy-to-Let
alternative_paths.description: Customer is purchasing a residential investment property to rent out. Affordability rules differ: rental income (typically 125–145% of mortgage payment at stressed rate) is primary affordability criterion rather than personal income. Stress test rate is higher (typically PRA-mandated).
key_differences: Affordability: rental income coverage ratio (not income multiples)
PRA SS13/16 underwriting standards for portfolio landlords (4+ mortgaged properties)

alternative_paths.name: Shared Ownership
alternative_paths.description: Customer purchases a share (typically 25–75%) of a property from a housing association, paying rent on the remaining share. Mortgage is only on the purchased share. Affordability assessment must consider both mortgage repayment and rental liability.
key_differences: Purchase price = share value only (not full property value)
Rent liability included in affordability assessment
Housing association as third party in completion
Staircasing provisions must be noted in mortgage offer

exception_paths.name: Down-Valuation
exception_paths.description: Valuation amount is less than the purchase price. The loan amount required may exceed the acceptable LTV against the surveyor's value. Customer options: renegotiate purchase price with vendor, increase deposit, or withdraw application.
resolution_options: Vendor reduces purchase price to match valuation
Customer increases deposit to maintain LTV within product limit
Customer withdraws application — valuation fee is typically non-refundable

exception_paths.name: Affordability Fail
exception_paths.description: Customer fails affordability assessment at DIP or full underwriting stage. Stress test at MCOB-prescribed rate results in monthly payment exceeding affordability threshold.
resolution_options: Decline issued — FOS signpost provided per Consumer Duty

exception_paths.name: Credit Decline
exception_paths.description: Credit score or credit history results in a decline at DIP or underwriting stage. Adverse credit history, CCJs, IVAs, or bankruptcy within defined look-back period.
resolution_options: FOS signpost and right to know (subject access right) provided
Customer directed to credit file provider to verify data accuracy

exception_paths.name: Fraud — Income Fabrication
exception_paths.description: Fraud detection or underwriter review identifies fabricated income documents (false payslips, P60 forgeries). Application immediately suspended. AML/fraud referral raised to SVC-014.
resolution_options: Application suspended and referred to Financial Crime team
SAR filed with NCA if suspicion of money laundering
Application declined; no FOS signpost in fraud decline

exception_paths.name: Property Chain Collapse
exception_paths.description: The property purchase chain collapses before exchange or completion. Mortgage offer may still be valid for the remaining validity period if the customer finds an alternative property.
resolution_options: Offer held open within 6-month validity window for alternative property
If new property: requires new valuation (PH-012 repeated)
If offer expires: new DIP or full application required
